text:
Carla: Quick heads-up — we’re cutting over the minimal/staging base-image + attestation webhook this Wed 09:00 PT. Main asks: 1) RBAC lock to prevent unrestricted image-push to staging, 2) KMS signing preflight (cosign), 3) audit log path + retention for any pushed artifacts. Planning doc: https://rwd.internal/runbook/staging-attest (draft).

Mike: Ack. For RBAC, are we doing a new clusterrole that only the pipeline service account can use, or adding a mutating admission gate?

Carla: New clusterrole + namespace-scoped binding for now. Mutating admission is long-term. Need SRE to approve the binding TTL and who can elevate. Suggested role: `image-pusher-staging` that grants `create` on `images` and `update` only for `staging/*` repos.

Sophia: For vuln triage: do we want an explicit canary tag sequence so we can rollback quickly if a CVE regression is detected? I can wire the eval harness to smoke test top-10 prompts.

Carla: Yes — canary tag = `sha:canary-20250310`. Run smoke eval + fuzzing. If token-level latency regresses >10% or quality drop on evalset, auto-fail promotion.

Owen: Audit path: pipeline will POST provenance to internal-elk -> index `artifacts-staging-*`. Need retention policy (90d?) and a signed-entry schema: `{ signer, image_digest, timestamp, build_id, scm_ref }`. Also add a cloudtrail mapping for KMS ops.

Mike: For KMS: cosign + KMS-backed key. If we rotate the signer key mid-canary, how do we validate old signatures? Do we keep previous public keys in the keyring?

Carla: We keep an allowlist of historical verification keys in the attestor service for the current rollout window (30d). Rotation plan: publish `key-v2` and keep `key-v1` for verification for 30d. After 30d, key-v1 is removed from verification list. Doc in runbook.

Sophia: Thumbs-up. Who owns the RBAC change? I can own the smoke tests and eval automation.

Mike: I’ll own RBAC changes + the k8s manifests. Plan to open PR tomorrow. Will add an approval step requiring two approvers from `eng-sre` or `eng-security` before merge.

Owen: I’ll wire the audit index + retention. Also adding an ELK alert on any push that doesn’t include `provenance` metadata.

deploy-bot: CI build 4789 passed for `staging/base:minimal-20250310` — signatures: cosign OK, sbom attached.

Carla: Nice. Two quick risk notes: 1) If RBAC is too strict we’ll break manual dev pushes; include a short-lived 'dev-temp' binding for ad-hoc tests. 2) Make sure the attestation webhook has a soft-fail mode for the first 24h to avoid blocking all pushes.

Mike: Will include `dev-temp` with TTL=8h and add webhook soft-fail flag `--attest-mode=warn` for the first 24h after cutover.

Sophia: For vuln triage, I’ll schedule a 30m triage slot 2 hours after cutover to review any high/sev CVE hits from vulnerability scan. Adding `@carla` and `@mike` to the calendar invite.

Owen: Question: audit retention for legal compliance — is 90d enough, or do we need longer for some customers?

Carla: Default 90d; for customers with compliance contracts we’ll export a signed S3 bucket with 1y retention. Flag in repo metadata `compliance:export=true` when customer requires it.

Mike: PR link (draft): https://rwd.internal/pulls/2123 — contains Role, RoleBinding, webhook flags, and the canary image policy. Please review.

Carla: Action items summarized: 1) Mike — open and merge RBAC PR w/ approvers, add dev-temp TTL. 2) Owen — ELK index + alert, cloudtrail KMS mapping. 3) Sophia — smoke + vuln-eval automation + triage slot. 4) Carla — publish key-rotation window & update runbook.

Sophia: :thumbsup:

Mike: Will push updates by EOD PST.

Owen: I’ll start ELK plumbing now, ping when PR is ready for the alert mapping.

Carla: If anything blocks, escalate in this thread. Otherwise proceed with the Wed 09:00 PT cutover plan. Thanks all. :party_popper:
